analyst_view.overall: Auxerre are 15th with 11 points under Will Still and drew 1-1 at Monaco last Saturday, leading through Romain Faivre and defending deep behind keeper Paul Nardi until an 83rd-minute equaliser. Marseille are 5th with 18 points but lost 3-2 at home to Le Mans on Sunday, ending five league wins in a row, and they host Levski Sofia in the Europa League tonight, so they come to Auxerre with about two and a half days' rest. New this week: Timothy Weah and Geoffrey Kondogbia, both starters against Le Mans, were left out of the Levski squad with no reason given (several outlets), so they may also miss Sunday; Hojbjerg, ill for Le Mans, is back, while Emerson and Cornelius are still out (both in the numbers). For Auxerre, top scorer Danny Namaso's injury is already counted (about -17% on their goals). Referee Francois Letexier (4.0 cards a game) is already counted; news for this match itself was thin three days out, with no full preview yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, Marseille 1.6 and Auxerre 1.2; they already take Namaso off Auxerre and add a little for Emerson missing from Marseille's defence. Possible absences of Weah and Kondogbia and a Thursday game could weaken Marseille's defence but also blunt their attack, and nothing is confirmed for Sunday, so I stay at about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, already lowered because both sides have won few corners lately (Auxerre 17 in their last 6). Auxerre defended deep and well at Monaco and Marseille usually have the ball away from home; that style is in the counts, so I stay at about 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, with referee Letexier adding about 3% and Marseille's calmer recent count trimming a little. Auxerre fighting near the drop and Marseille after a painful home defeat could make it tense, but that is ordinary for this fixture, so I stay at about 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.2 shots, 12.8 for Marseille and 11.4 for Auxerre, already raising Auxerre for how many shots Marseille have conceded lately (91 in 6). Tired legs after Thursday could blunt Marseille a little while giving Auxerre more room, so the two roughly cancel and I stay at about 24.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target, already lowering Marseille (21 on target in their last 6) and raising Auxerre against Marseille's open defence. Gouiri leads Marseille's attack and Auxerre rely on Archer and Faivre with Namaso out, which the numbers know, so I stay at about 9.1.
